subject.title: fix(agents): collect unreachable transcript branches during compaction rotation

question: Should compaction rotation intentionally omit unreachable sibling branches from successor files and rely on the linked predecessor file for complete historical branch data?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and fixes unbounded carry-forward, but it deliberately reverses previously tested retention behavior; source and tests cannot determine whether successor-local branch browsing remains a desired product contract.

options.title: Use active-lineage successors
options.body: Approve the patch’s model: successor files retain active ancestry and globally consumed metadata, while predecessor files retain full inactive branch history.

options.title: Preserve successor branch history
options.body: Require a different bounded representation that keeps sibling branches directly available in each successor without carrying their full dead payload forward.

recommendation.title: Use active-lineage successors
recommendation.body: Approve the patch’s model: successor files retain active ancestry and globally consumed metadata, while predecessor files retain full inactive branch history.

likelyOwner.reason: They co-authored and reviewed the original rotation feature and are the strongest available history-based owner for its intended retention contract.
